english: Let $C$ be the curve $\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}:y^{3}+3y=2x\}$, and let $P$ be the point of $C$ with abscissa $7$. If $O$ is the origin, then the area of the region bounded by $C$ and the line segment $OP$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $C$ वक्र $\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}:y^{3}+3y=2x\}$ है तथा $P$ वक्र $C$ का वह बिन्दु है जिसका भुज $7$ है। यदि $O$ मूलबिन्दु है, तो $C$ तथा रेखाखण्ड $OP$ द्वारा परिबद्ध क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल बराबर है
solution: $x=\dfrac{y^{3}+3y}{2}$ is increasing in $y$, so each $x$ gives one point of $C$; at $x=7$: $y^{3}+3y=14\Rightarrow y=2$, $P(7,2)$.
$OP$: $x=\dfrac{7y}{2}$. For $0\le y\le 2$: $\dfrac{7y}{2}-\dfrac{y^{3}+3y}{2}=\dfrac{y(4-y^{2})}{2}\ge 0$, so $OP$ lies to the right of $C$.
solution_full: $C$ cannot be written easily as $y=f(x)$, but it is $x=g(y)=\dfrac{y^{3}+3y}{2}$ with $g'(y)=\dfrac{3y^{2}+3}{2}>0$, so $g$ is strictly increasing and $C$ meets every vertical line exactly once.
For $x=7$: $y^{3}+3y-14=0\Rightarrow (y-2)(y^{2}+2y+7)=0$, and the quadratic has no real root, so $P=(7,2)$.
Between the two: $\dfrac{7y}{2}-g(y)=\dfrac{7y-y^{3}-3y}{2}=\dfrac{y(2-y)(2+y)}{2}\ge 0$ on $[0,2]$, zero only at $y=0,2$. So $C$ and $OP$ meet only at $O$ and $P$ and bound one region.
(Check: the area between $C$, the $x$-axis and $x=7$ is $14-\int_{0}^{2}g(y)dy=14-5=9$, the triangle under $OP$ has area $7$, and $9-7=2$.)
originality_note: New: a curve given only implicitly (y^3 + 3y = 2x) that is a function of y, cut by the chord from O to the point with abscissa 7 (way 5). Closest known: area under the inverse of x^3 + x. Different because: the region is a curve-chord region, and the y-integration is forced because y(x) has no usable closed form.

concept_use.Area obtained by integrating with respec: The curve is x = (y^3+3y)/2; the area is the integral of 7y/2 - (y^3+3y)/2 over 0 <= y <= 2.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve and symbol introduced, region named by its bounding curves, one reading, answer unique and equal to the plan; options of one form; Hindi mirrors the English maths. Checked that the cubic in y has the single real root y = 2 at x = 7, so P is unique; distractors 5, 7, 9 are the integral of g, the triangle and the area under C. No change.
key_step: Recognise C as x = g(y) and integrate the horizontal width between the chord and the curve.
justification: Needs the decision to integrate in y plus a routine root and integral; three routine steps with no insight, like 2021-P1-Q2 (L2).
blueprint_concepts: Area obtained by integrating with respect to y
